title: TraceSampler: Making Sampling Errors Predictable and Correctable for Accelerated Generative Sampling
abstract: Accurate sampling from continuous-time generative models can require many model evaluations. Low-step sampling reduces cost, but coarse updates introduce endpoint errors that can accumulate and degrade generation quality. We introduce TraceSampler, a post-training method that corrects these errors without modifying the pretrained model. Rather than optimising low-step updates directly, TraceSampler models endpoint error as a sample-specific prediction problem. A higher-step reference integration over the same interval provides the supervised target, while a compact representation makes high-dimensional error predictable from the sampling trace. This representation combines shared residual structure, trace-derived directions, and a low-rank remainder, so shallow per-step MLP heads predict sample-dependent coefficients. These coefficients drive a two-stage learned residual correction: the first stage predicts the full endpoint residual, while an intermediate backbone evaluation provides new trace information to predict the remaining residual; this evaluation is reused by the following step. TraceSampler is evaluated with Rectified Flow on CIFAR-10, SiT-XL/2 on ImageNet-256, and SD3.5 Medium for text-to-image generation. At 10 steps, it reduces trajectory MSE relative to matched-step Euler by 90.5% on CIFAR-10 and 85.6% on ImageNet-256, while achieving FID scores of 2.692 and 2.189, close to 120-step Heun references of 2.601 and 2.056 with 24$\times$ fewer backbone evaluations. On SD3.5 Medium, TraceSampler improves image quality and prompt following; at 10 steps, ImageReward rises from 0.752 to 0.906 while trajectory MSE falls by 70.7%. These gains preserve Euler's backbone-evaluation budget, add less than 0.4% inference FLOPs, and incur negligible wall-clock overhead, showing that coarse-step sampling error can be made predictable from the sampling trace and efficiently corrected.

title: Host-Aware Web Crawling for LLM Pretraining Data
abstract: Web crawling is a major source of large language model (LLM) pretraining data, yet data-selection pipelines discard a large share of crawled pages. We investigate how a crawler should allocate its budget across and within hosts to collect more high-quality pretraining data. Combining document-level quality classifier scores, web-graph centrality metrics, and Common Crawl's per-host crawl coverage, we find that roughly half of the variation in classifier scores occurs between hosts. In the crawls we analyze, a few pages from a host also provide a useful estimate of the quality of its remaining pages. Common Crawl uses harmonic centrality, a graph centrality metric, to guide its crawl allocation. In our simulations, using centrality to choose which hosts to crawl yields limited gains over random ordering and performs worse for some classifiers. For deciding how deeply to crawl each host, sampling a few pages and then fetching more from hosts with higher-scoring samples collects several times more high-quality pages per fetch than uniform depth or centrality-based allocation. Finally, Common Crawl's observed per-host coverage has little correlation with the evaluated quality signals. We estimate that tens of millions of high-quality pages remain among known but uncrawled URLs in each crawl examined, with most concentrated on a small share of hosts.

title: Robust Langevin Sampling under State-Dependent Heavy-Tailed Noise with Applications to LLM Fine-Tuning
abstract: Existing convergence guarantees for non-log-concave sampling with stochastic gradient Langevin Monte Carlo (SG-LMC) typically assume globally Lipschitz gradients and uniformly bounded noise variance. Both assumptions can fail even in elementary sampling problems, and relaxing them better reflects practical applications such as Bayesian fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). We relax both assumptions through generalized smoothness and our proposed state-dependent heavy-tailed oracle with finite $p$-th moments, $1<p\leq 2$. The oracle permits infinite variance when $p<2$ and includes the Blum-Gladyshev (BG-0) condition. We study these relaxations separately and jointly, proposing three methods. Under globally Lipschitz gradients, robust LMC (R-LMC) handles the proposed oracle through geometric-median centering and residual clipping. With exact gradients, adaptive LMC (A-LMC) controls discretization error under generalized smoothness. Robust adaptive LMC (RA-LMC) addresses both relaxations through robust estimation and a noise-aware step size. For all three methods, we establish non-asymptotic convergence guarantees in Fisher information (FI) without assuming dissipativity or a functional inequality. Synthetic experiments demonstrate FI convergence and the benefit of each mechanism. Bayesian fine-tuning experiments with LLMs and vision-language models support our oracle model and show that RA-LMC matches or outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

title: Guide pour une intégration réussie de l’IA au sein des organisations
abstract: Plusieurs organisations (publiques, privées et à but non lucratif) ont intégré des outils d’IA dans leurs activités ou sont en train de se familiariser avec ceux-ci. Cependant, de nombreuses études montrent que, malgré des attentes élevées et des investissements importants, la plupart d’entre elles n’ont pas encore constaté de gains mesurables en matière de productivité, de chiffre d’affaires ou de retour sur investissement. Le retour sur investissement peut tarder à se concrétiser, puisque les grandes innovations technologiques mettent souvent plus de dix ans à produire des retombées économiques mesurables. L’objectif de ce guide est de fournir aux organisations des stratégies pour intégrer avec succès les outils d’IA et de proposer de bonnes pratiques permettant d’utiliser ces outils de manière efficace et responsable. La version préliminaire du guide s’appuie sur une revue des lignes directrices, des cadres et des guides sur l’intégration de l’IA publiés par des organisations publiques, privées et à but non lucratif au Canada et à l’international, ainsi que sur des études scientifiques récentes. Le guide a ensuite été bonifié à partir des résultats de l'étude, qui repose sur des données recueillies auprès de gestionnaires, de développeurs et de formateurs de quatre secteurs au Québec : l’économie sociale et l’action communautaire, la finance, les ressources humaines et les technologies de l’information.

title: Convergence Between Artificial Intelligence and Digital Purchasing Behavior
authors: Célia Maria Ramos Serra Reis Barroso
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming digital behavior and consumer decision-making, reshaping interactions between individuals and brands across digital platforms. This chapter analyzes the relationship between digital behavior, AI, and marketing strategies in a changing technological context. It examines how AI-driven tools, such as predictive analytics and automated recommendation systems, enable content personalization, improve user experiences, and increase marketing effectiveness. Based on contemporary literature and secondary data from sources including Statista, Pew Research Center, Pordata and Euromonitor, the study adopts an exploratory approach to assess AI's impact on consumer engagement and strategic marketing practices. It also discusses ethical challenges, such as data privacy, algorithmic bias, and manipulation risks. The research offers insights for scholars and practitioners on AI's growing influence and highlights the need for future qualitative studies on consumer perceptions.

title: A Hybrid deep learning model for effective segmentation and classification of lung nodules from CT images
abstract: Deep learning algorithms will be used to detect lung nodule anomalies at an earlier stage. The primary goal of this effort is to properly identify lung cancer, which is critical in preserving a person’s life. Lung cancer has been a source of concern for people all around the world for decades. Several researchers presented numerous issues and solutions for various stages of a computer-aided system for diagnosing lung cancer in its early stages, as well as information about lung cancer. Computer vision is one of the field of artificial intelligence this is a better way to detect and prevent the lung cancer. This study focuses on the stages involved in detecting lung tumor regions, namely pre-processing, segmentation, and classification models. An adaptive median filter is used in pre-processing to identify the noise. The work’s originality seeks to create a simple yet effective model for the rapid identification and U-net architecture based segmentation of lung nodules. This approach focuses on the identification and segmentation of lung cancer by detecting picture normalcy and abnormalities.

title: Role-Guided Risk-Aware Attention for Multi-AUV Target-Zone Reaching under Active Defense
abstract: Cooperative target-zone reaching by multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) under active defense remains challenging because each vehicle must make sequential guidance decisions under nonlinear hydrodynamics, sonar-limited perception, obstacle constraints, and defender interference. This paper proposes a role-guided risk-aware attention variant of multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG), termed role-guided risk-aware attention MADDPG (RGRA-MADDPG), for attacker-side multi-AUV target-zone reaching under active defense. Different from homogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) policies, the proposed method assigns mission-specific roles to the AUVs, including a Primary Attack AUV, a Coordinated Strike AUV, and a Bait AUV. A role-conditioned attention module is developed to help each AUV selectively emphasize targets, defenders, obstacles, and teammates from local observations, while a risk-prior bias introduces interpretable obstacle-, defender-, and target-related cues into the attention scores. The framework is trained under centralized training and executed through decentralized local policies. Comparative simulations, perturbation tests, mechanism-isolation studies, and physical-response validation are used to evaluate target-reaching success, cooperative behavior, robustness, and command feasibility. Results show that the proposed method improves adversarial target-zone reaching performance over standard MADDPG-based variants while producing differentiated and interpretable multi-AUV tactics.

title: Real-Time Traffic Density Estimation: A Hybrid Computer Vision and Predictive Machine Learning Pipeline
abstract: Traffic density estimation from camera feeds requires connecting visual perception with short-horizon forecasting. We present a two-stage pipeline that combines vehicle detection and tracking with a spatial logic layer, followed by a temporal estimator. The spatial layer filters bounding boxes by their overlap with a precomputed road mask and extracts per-frame traffic features. LSTM, GRU, and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) estimators use these features to predict five future steps from a ten-frame input window. We benchmark ten detector variants from six families on a dataset of 5,716 annotated frames using a single NVIDIA GPU. YOLOv5l achieves the highest mAP@50:95 of 0.524 at 56 frames per second, while YOLOv8n reaches 258 frames per second at 0.487 mAP@50:95; these rates measure detector inference without tracking or spatial filtering. Temporal evaluation on 29,243 held-out windows yields aggregate R-squared values of 0.858 for GRU, 0.856 for LSTM, and 0.840 for TCN. These metrics measure forecasts of detector-derived telemetry and are dominated by direction variance, rather than establishing absolute traffic-density accuracy. No road mask was available for the evaluation stream, limiting validation of the spatial filtering component. A live run on a third camera stream examines forecasting behavior within the complete pipeline. The results characterize detector speed-accuracy trade-offs and the limitations of short-window traffic telemetry forecasting.

title: SBNO : Schrödinger Bridge Neural Operator for the Forward and Inverse Problems under Missing Information
abstract: Partial differential equation (PDE) surrogate modeling often relies on either dense observations or access to governing equations/physics constraints. In practice, observations can be sparse and partial, and the underlying physics may be partially specified or unavailable. We introduce SBNO, an equation-free paired-data diffusion bridge matching framework that learns conditional operators for both forward and inverse PDE problems under partial observations. SBNO uses diffusion Schrödinger bridge matching to learn a pair of time-dependent drifts from a mask-aware endpoint coupling that preserves empirical input-solution pairing during training and supports both PDE-task directions within a single framework. At inference time, SBNO produces a deterministic point reconstruction by integrating the probability-flow ODE constructed from the learned drift pair, without inference-time observation or PDE guidance-weight tuning. On five PDE benchmarks with 5% observations, SBNO achieves superior or comparable accuracy to baselines while demonstrating lower test-instance error dispersion. Furthermore, SBNO is at least $9.7 \times$ faster and reduces GPU memory by at least $4.3 \times$ compared to guided-diffusion baselines.

title: A robust digital receiver architecture for continuous-variable quantum key distribution
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution utilizes advanced digital signal processing techniques to mitigate channel impairments, driving the progress of high-performance quantum secure communications. Specifically, digital heterodyne receivers are commonly implemented using down-conversion algorithms to detect both components simultaneously where the signal is modulated onto an intermediate frequency to avoid low-frequency noise and bypass stringent optical phase-locking requirements. However, a rigorous analysis of the quantum security implications of the digital down-conversion algorithm remains absent. In this paper, we investigate the algorithm process from the perspective of quantum operator evolution, revealing that the frequency folding effect inherent in down-conversion inevitably mixes the image-frequency information into the baseband signal. To address this issue, we propose a novel operator reconstruction detection scheme based on dual-path digital heterodyne receiver. By performing a non-equal weighted combination of the output operators along two optical paths in the digital domain, this scheme perfectly cancels out the image-frequency operator physically. The robust receiver architecture preserves the baseband noise-suppression advantages, inherently achieves perfect mode balancing for asymmetric optical detection losses, and fundamentally closes the image-frequency crosstalk. Practical experiments have validated the feasibility of the proposed architecture and its effective suppression of image-frequency noise, achieving a performance of 11.4 Mbps @ 42 km. This work lays a solid theoretical and algorithmic foundation for future high-performance, highly secure digital continuous-variable quantum key distribution systems.

title: Volume Rendering with Metric--Phase Fields for Thin Structures and Sign-Ambiguous Geometry
abstract: Neural implicit surface methods that couple volume rendering with signed distance functions (SDFs), such as VolSDF and NeuS, achieve high-quality multi-view reconstruction for watertight objects. However, these approaches rely on a globally consistent inside-outside partition of space. This assumption becomes fragile for thin structures (e.g., sheets, tubes, and thin walls) and can break down for sign-ambiguous geometry (e.g., surfaces with boundary, non-manifold junctions, and closely spaced surface components), often resulting in spurious closures or loss of fine structures. Unsigned distance field (UDF) formulations relax the global sign requirement and better support non-watertight geometry, but are substantially harder to optimize. We propose PhaseSurf, a neural volume rendering framework built on Metric-Phase Fields (MPFs). MPFs decompose geometry into a nonnegative metric field capturing unsigned proximity and a continuous phase field providing a soft sign cue. By coupling the two through residual phase injection, MPFs yield a signed composite implicit function with stable near-surface gradients while retaining UDF-like robustness in sign-ambiguous regions. This design enables direct iso-surface extraction using standard Marching Cubes and avoids the failure modes of both pure SDF- and UDF-based formulations. We further introduce MPF-specific training losses that enforce metric consistency, stabilize phase transitions near the interface, and suppress spurious geometry in free space. Experiments on multi-view datasets with thin structures and sign-ambiguous geometry show that PhaseSurf produces more stable reconstructions and higher-quality geometry than UDF-based methods and recent 3DGS pipelines, while avoiding artifacts typical of SDF-based approaches.

title: EXPERIMENTAL COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF NAIVE BAYES AND RULE BASED DECISION TREE PERFORMANCE IN ATTRIBUTIVE CLASSIFICATION OF SCHOLARLY ARTICLES
abstract: Document classification categorizes documents based on their attributes or contents to determine how they will be stored, retrieved, and shared. Improper classification of documents can lead to significant waste of time, resources, productivity, and efficiency in organizational information management systems. This study presents the Experimental Comparative Analysis (ECA) of Naive Bayes Model (NBM) and Rule-Based Decision Tree Model (RBDTM) in the classification of journal articles based on their attributes such as Name of Journal (NOJ) regarded as the specific domain, Peer Reviewed (PR) status, Volume Information (VI), the Title (T), Author Names (AN), Digital Object Identifier (DOI) and Keywords (KW). The models were trained based on direct algebraic solutions, saved parameters, and deterministic passes without gradient descent updates, using supervised Machine Learning (ML) approach and K-fold validation sampling technique for training and testing. Performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1-score, program execution time, information retrieval response time, memory usage, and confusion matrix were used for analysis and evaluation. The training and testing datasets were obtained from open-licensed, peer-reviewed journal articles from Africa, Asia, the United States of America, Eastern and Western Europe. The average test results at the baseline threshold showed that the NBM performed better than the RBDTM in accuracy, recall, and F1-score (68%, 68%, and 80.6%, respectively); both models achieved 100% precision and 0% specificity. In contrast, RBDTM outperformed NBM in program execution time, information retrieval response time, and memory usage (17.19ms, 7.44ms, and 0.13%, respectively). At the optimized threshold, both models tied with 100% accuracy, 100% precision, 100% recall, 0% specificity, and 100% F1-score, but the RBDTM demonstrated the best overall performance with 18.2ms program execution time, 7.74ms information retrieval response time, and 0.14% memory usage.

title: Code and data for "Physically constrained adversarial attacks on neural-network classifiers of quantum phases: symmetry-breaking versus topological order"
abstract: Simulation code, generated datasets, trained network weights, raw results files and figure scripts accompanying the manuscript “Physically constrained adversarial attacks on neural-network classifiers of quantum phases: symmetry-breaking versus topological order”, submitted to Quantum Frontiers. Contents: Monte Carlo generation of two-dimensional Ising configurations (L = 16); generation of Su–Schrieffer–Heeger chains (N = 96) with chiral-symmetric hopping disorder and real-space winding number; MLP, periodic CNN and Z2-symmetrised CNN classifiers; FGSM/PGD, greedy spin-flip and Hamiltonian-level hopping-disorder attacks; adversarial training; and all results from which the figures and tables in the paper are produced. See README.md for the file list and reproduction steps. Tested with Python 3.13, NumPy 2.5, SciPy 1.18, PyTorch 2.14 (CPU) and Matplotlib 3.11.

title: QuantumShield AI: An AI-Powered Post-Quantum Cryptography Recommendation Platform
abstract: The finalization of the NIST post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), with FN-DSA (draft FIPS 206), has shifted the migration question from whether to adopt PQC to which standard best fits an organization's operational and regulatory context. Existing studies benchmark these algorithms thoroughly but stop short of a selection mechanism, leaving practitioners to interpret timing tables by hand. This paper presents QuantumShield AI, a decision-support platform that formalizes PQC algorithm selection as a multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) problem, encodes the selection task as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO), and solves it with the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on a statevector simulator, cross-validated by an exact classical solver. Six industry profiles — banking, healthcare, IoT/edge, government, e-commerce, and defense supply criteria weightings grounded in sector requirements. The framework is delivered as a three-tier platform combining a React front end, a Spring Boot service layer with JWT-based role-controlled access, and a Python/Qiskit quantum microservice over PostgreSQL. To our knowledge this is the first framework to operationalize selection across the complete finalized NIST portfolio, converting sector requirements into an auditable, reproducible recommendation. Across all six profiles the QAOA solution recovers the exact optimum (approximation ratio = 1.0), validating the pipeline; we are explicit that at the four-algorithm scale this certifies correctness rather than quantum advantage, and the QUBO–QAOA formulation is carried as a forward-compatible path to NP-hard enterprise-portfolio selection. The contribution is a novel, deployable decision methodology and its engineered realization.

title: Field Notes from a Low-Cost Robot Learning Lab: Hardware Churn, Software Whiplash, and What Actually Went Wrong
abstract: This is the informal companion to two more rigorous papers from the same project. Over roughly seven weeks we trained imitation-learning policies on a self-built SO-101 robot arm, and along the way we moved the work between machines more often than planned, rebuilt the camera setup, fought a fast-moving open-source framework, and lost an embarrassing amount of time to causes that turned out to be a loose power cable, a swapped port, or a missing audio package. The quantified findings are reported elsewhere. title: Identifiability Under Runtime Shielding
abstract: This methods note examines what can be inferred about an agent when a runtime safety shield mediates its proposed actions. Different proposals can produce identical safe executions, so agreement in executed behaviour does not necessarily imply agreement in proposal distributions. Conversely, distinguishable proposal distributions do not by themselves identify a unique internal mechanism or establish its causal contribution. Three elementary propositions address conditional safety invariance, observational collapse under shielding, and restricted injectivity on a declared family of proposal distributions. Worked examples explain why an intervention witness may remain insufficient, why full channel rank does not guarantee useful finite-sample discrimination, and why observations that are individually innocuous may jointly disclose sensitive information. PDE-DI is presented as a measurement procedure for documenting the target contrast, permitted probes and observations, execution semantics, channel calibration, disclosure constraints, uncertainty, and interpretation limits. It distinguishes executed violations, disallowed proposals, and mediator interventions. Unidentifiability or inadequate measurement precision must not be interpreted as equivalence or a negative causal finding. Causal attribution requires a separate design with justified interventions, appropriate comparisons, and an explicit causal estimand. The reported technical evidence is a finite reference program that enumerates 2,187 trajectories and 13,122 transitions and checks seven mathematical assertion groups. These are reference checks, not independent empirical trials. The program contains no developmental learning, autonomous agent, or Purple implementation. The literature discussion is a targeted comparison with 30 references and explicitly stated source-access limitations. Appendix A outlines the Purple developmental research programme as a possible future application, including untested hypotheses and requirements for a valid component-effect study. The supported contribution is an explicit, worked measurement framework based on established arguments. No new general theorem, empirical superiority, distinctive Purple functionality, or mechanistic novelty is established. This record contains the English and Hungarian manuscripts, version 0.3, dated 9 October 2026. The manuscripts disclose generative AI assistance in drafting, translation, and consistency checking.

abstract: The geopolitical issue between Israel and Palestine has sparked a wide range of public reactions on social media, particularly on the platform X. Sentiment analysis is a widely discussed topic in Natural Language Processing.This study develops a sentiment classification model for that issue using the BERT Base Uncased architecture, with data labeled automatically through the VADER approach.Data were collected via scraping with Tweet-Harvest, yielding 3,172 tweets, later reduced to 2,362 after preprocessing stages including cleaning, case folding, tokenizing, stopword removal, and stemming.VADER labeling produced a distribution of 73.7% negative sentiment and 26.3% positive sentiment.The model achieved 87.34% accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-Score for the negative class of 92%, 90%, and 91%, respectively, while the positive class obtained 74%, 79%, and 77%.The macro-average F1-score reached 84%, reflecting the model's performance across both classes with equal weighting despite the imbalanced data distribution.These results indicate that BERT Base Uncased can classify VADER-generated labels with fairly good performance in the context of international geopolitical issues.Kata

title: Probabilistic Forecasting of Electric Vehicle Charging in a Time-varying Hierarchical Infrastructure
abstract: Uncertainty quantification for electric vehicle (EV) charging demand is essential to turn the increasing pressure of EV adoption on power systems into a source of flexibility. We study a large-scale dataset of public charging stations in Scotland, where demand exhibits a hierarchical structure, organized across multiple aggregation levels, from individual charging points to regional and national scales. The charging infrastructure is continuously evolving, with new stations deployed and existing ones occasionally removed, which calls for forecasting and uncertainty quantification methods tailored to this evolving structure. To address these challenges, we combine hierarchical forecasting with recent advances in conformal prediction with missing data. The conformal procedures considered produce valid prediction intervals at every node of the hierarchy and the algorithm CP-MNR-Nested successfully accounts for the time-varying hierarchical structure of the data.

title: The Limits of Query Monitoring against Distributed Model Extraction
abstract: Model providers now face distillation campaigns run through thousands of accounts, each of which looks like an ordinary user. When network and payment metadata cannot link those accounts, the only evidence left is what they ask. We study what a provider can and cannot learn from those queries alone, using one million real chat turns for development and 17 later weeks that no design choice touched for a single frozen evaluation. The answer is set less by anything specific to extraction than by benign coordination: a campaign is visible only if it is more distinctive than the most distinctive group of ordinary users in the same week. We make this precise, show that a small but positive difference between campaign and users buys a detection time rather than detectability, and identify the campaign that is hardest to detect. Empirically, a calibrated monitor catches naive distributed extraction that per-account monitors miss (0.86-1.00 of weeks), and one variant - selecting accounts that move together after discounting how topical each one is - still catches campaigns padded with natural text (0.50-0.96 of weeks) where the other two spectral detectors catch none. Distilling each campaign into a small student shows that, in our testbed, campaigns that evaded every detector kept at most 42% of the capability of a detectable one. The limits are equally concrete: a campaign that ramps up slowly poisons every detector's calibration, benign evaluation pipelines look exactly like distillation, we found no deployable detector at colluder shares of 2.5% or below, and campaigns that relay real users' requests may be invisible to any query-only monitor.

title: Quantum Information-Theoretic Analysis of Optical Fiber Sensing via Stimulated Brillouin Scattering
abstract: Stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) is a powerful mechanism for distributed sensing in optical fibers, as the Brillouin response is highly sensitive to local material parameters. Assuming the input probe is a quantum state, we develop a quantum-information-theoretic framework for SBS-based fiber sensing and intrusion detection. Starting from a linearized opto-acoustic Hamiltonian, we derive an effective input-output relation for a short fiber segment. We then model each fiber segment as a single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel and the entire fiber as a cascade of quantum channels. We then compute the quantum Fisher information for general SBS-dependent parameters and identify optimal measurement settings to achieve the quantum limit, comparing them with receiver-constrained strategies such as heterodyne detection and photon counting. In addition, we propose an adaptive approach that achieves first-order asymptotic optimality and provides a novel second-order correction to address preliminary miscalibration. As an application, we apply the framework to the fiber-tapping detection problem.

title: Unreliable Narrator Framing as a Cost-effective Mechanism for Satire Explanation of Australian and American Satirical News
abstract: Satirical news is a unique form of misinformation: it is intended to be humorous by the original publication source but can be misinterpreted. Explanation of satirical news articles is challenging because recent and local context needs to be incorporated. This is a pilot study that explores explanation generation for satirical news articles from Australia and compares them alongside those from USA. The paper demonstrates that framing explanations on unreliable narrator theory on open-weights models can be a feasible, cost-effective alternative to frontier models. We find that models identify the satirical tropes more accurately on the American source than the Australian one. This work results in a novel dataset and an evaluation benchmark for satirical explanation.

title: A Simple Explicit Construction of Smaller Strong Blocking Sets
abstract: Alon, Bishnoi, Das and Neri constructed sequences of strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space $P({\bf F}_q, k-1)$ with sizes at most $Cqk$, where $k$ goes to the infinity and $C$ is a fixed positive constant not depending on $q$, in their paper published in Transactions AMS, vol. 277, pp. 5389-5410, 2024. This is equivalent to a sequence of minimal $[n_i,k_i]_q$ codes with positive rate $\frac{k_i}{n_i} \geq c$, where $k_i$ goes to the infinity and $c$ is a fixed positive constant only depending on $q$. They solved one of the main open problems on minimal codes. The Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri construction was based on asymptotically good sequences of algebraic geometric codes and expander graphs. However, the constant $C$ is large for small prime power $q$. In this paper, based on a simple approach using $(q-1)$-power intersecting algebraic geometric codes via concatenation to construct minimal codes, we construct explicit strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space with sizes around $2(q^2-1)k$, equivalently, explicit minimal $[n,k]_q$ codes with length around $2(q^2-1)k$. This is an essential improvement on the previous result of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri, when $q \leq 11$. For large $q$, strong blocking sets and minimal codes in our construction are worse than the previous construction of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri. However, our approach is much simpler and does not depend on expander graphs.

title: التطبيقية: الإنتاجية الذكية وهندسة البرمجيات ChatGPTموسوعة
abstract: يقدم هذا المستند "موسوعة ChatGPT التطبيقية: الإنتاجية الذكية وهندسة البرمجيات" (من إعداد د. عابدة الحناوي) دليلاً علمياً وعملياً شاملاً لاستخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي وتطبيقاته في هندسة الأوامر، أتمتة المهام، ودورة تطوير البرمجيات. يتكون المرجع المرفق من أربعة أدلة علمية وتطبيقية رئيسية تغطي جوانب مختلفة لاستخدام ChatGPT والذكاء الاصطناعي: 1. دليل ChatGPT للاحتراف العملي (الدليل العام) يركز على إتقان الأساسيات وهندسة الأوامر واستخدام الميزات المتقدمة: المقدمة والأساسيات: التعريف بنموذج ChatGPT، كيفية إنشاء الحساب، الواجهة الرئيسية، الفرق بين النماذج المتوفرة ($GPT-4o$, $GPT-4o\ mini$, $o1-preview$, $o1-mini$) وإدارة المحادثات وتثبيتها. هندسة الأوامر (Prompt Engineering): القواعد الذهبية لصياغة الأوامر القوية ($Role$, $Context$, $Task$, $Format$, $Constraints$)، استخدام تقنيات $Few-Shot Examples$، التعديل التكراري، وتجنب الأخطاء الشائعة. الإبداع البصري عبر DALL-E: توليد الصور، ضبط الأساليب الفنية والإضاءة والزوايا، تعديل الصور وإضافة/حذف العناصر، وحالات الاستخدام في التصميم والتسويق. تحليل البيانات والملفات: رفع ملفات Excel وPDF، استخدام $Code Interpreter$ لتحليل البيانات وبناء المخططات البيانية، واستخراج البيانات المتقدمة. بناء مساعد مخصص (Custom GPTs): طريقة تصميم وتدريب مساعد خاص بك عبر رفع المعرفة والتعليمات الدقيقة وتفعيل القدرات والمشاركة. المهارات المتقدمة وحالات الاستخدام: استخدام التصفح التلقائي للويب، الذاكرة طويلة المدى، تنظيم المشاريع، واختصارات الإنتاجية، بالإضافة لتطبيقات عملية للكتّاب، الإعلاميين، والمسوقين. 2. دليل ChatGPT للبرمجة (للمطورين) مخصص لمهندسي البرمجيات لتعزيز الإنتاجية وكتابة الأكواد: الإعداد وصياغة أوامر الكود: تخصيص $Custom\ Instructions$ للبرمجة، اختيار النموذج الأنسب للكود المعقد أو السريع، وصياغة الأوامر البرمجية الاحترافية. توليد الأكواد وإكمالها: توليد الدوال والوحدات البرمجية، التحويل بين لغات البرمجة المختلفة (مثل Python إلى Go أو Rust)، شرح الكود المعقد وتوليد هيكل المشاريع ($Boilerplate$) والتطبيقات الكاملة. التنقيح ومراجعة الكود (Debugging & Review): تحليل رسائل الأخطاء، إيجاد السبب الجذري للـ Bugs، المراجعة الأمنية للكشف عن ثغرات OWASP، وتحليل وتعقيد الأداء ($Big\ O$). الاختبارات وجودة الكود: كتابة اختبارات الوحدات ($Unit\ Tests$) بـ pytest، اختبار الحالات الحدية ($Edge\ Cases$)، وتحليل التغطية ($Coverage\ Analysis$). إعادة الهيكلة والأتمتة: تطبيق أنماط التصميم ($Design\ Patterns$)، إعادة الهيكلة الذكية، وأتمتة سير العمل البرمجي ($CI/CD\ Pipelines$, $Pre-commit\ hooks$). 3. دليل ChatGPT للإضافات وبروتوكول MCP يشرح ربط الذكاء الاصطناعي بالأدوات والأنظمة الخارجية: مقدمة في MCP والإضافات: مفهوم بروتوكول context Model Protocol (MCP) والفرق بينه وبين $Plugins$ و$Custom\ GPTs$. إعداد وتثبيت MCP: متطلبات النظام، ضبط ملف التكوين $mcp.json$، وربط الخوادم بالتطبيقات وإدارتها. استخدام خوادم MCP الجاهزة: الاتصال بنظام الملفات المحلي ($Filesystem$)، قواعد البيانات (PostgreSQL/SQLite)، مستودعات GitHub، والتطبيقات مثل Slack وGoogle Drive. بناء خوادم MCP مخصصة: هيكل الخادم، كتابة الأدوات ($Tools$)، الاختبار بـ $MCP\ Inspector$، والتكامل المؤسسي وأفضل ممارسات الأمان. 4. دليل ChatGPT للوكلاء الأذكياء (AI Agents) يركز على بناء أنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي المستقلة القادرة على التخطيط والتنفيذ: مفهوم الوكلاء الأذكياء: الفرق بين $Agent$ و$Chatbot$، أنواع الوكلاء، واستعراض أطر العمل الشهيرة مثل CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph, وOpenAI Swarm. هيكل الوكيل وأدواته: مكونات العقل ($LLM$)، الأدوات ($Tools$)، أنواع الذاكرة (قليلة وطويلة المدى)، وحلقة التخطيط واتخاذ القرار ($ReAct\ Loop$). بناء وكيل من الصفر: إعداد البيئة بـ Python، كتابة الأدوات، تنفيذ حلقة $ReAct$، والاختبار والنشر. أنظمة الوكلاء المتعددة (Multi-Agent Systems): أنماط التعاون بين عدة وكلاء ($Sequential$, $Manager-Worker$, $Parallel$, $Debate$)، والتطبيق العملي باستخدام إطار CrewAI. النشر والمراقبة والسلامة: أتمتة المهام، وضع حدود الأمان والحماية ($Guardrails$)، ومراقبة التكاليف والأداء في بيئة الإنتاج.

GPTs): طريقة تصميم وتدريب مساعد خاص بك عبر رفع المعرفة والتعليمات الدقيقة وتفعيل القدرات والمشاركة. المهارات المتقدمة وحالات الاستخدام: استخدام التصفح التلقائي للويب، الذاكرة طويلة المدى، تنظيم المشاريع، واختصارات الإنتاجية، بالإضافة لتطبيقات عملية للكتّاب، الإعلاميين، والمسوقين. 2. دليل ChatGPT للبرمجة (للمطورين) مخصص لمهندسي البرمجيات لتعزيز الإنتاجية وكتابة الأكواد: الإعداد وصياغة أوامر الجذري للـ Bugs، المراجعة الأمنية للكشف عن ثغرات OWASP، وتحليل وتعقيد الأداء ($Big\ O$). الاختبارات وجودة الكود: كتابة اختبارات الوحدات ($Unit\ Tests$) بـ pytest، اختبار الحالات الحدية ($Edge\ الأمان. 4. دليل ChatGPT للوكلاء الأذكياء (AI Agents) يركز على بناء أنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي المستقلة القادرة على التخطيط والتنفيذ: مفهوم الوكلاء الأذكياء: الفرق بين $Agent$ و$Chatbot$، أنواع الوكلاء، title: Error Propagation in AI Models: How Small Mistakes Accumulate, Spread and Grow
abstract: This presentation examines the mechanisms through which errors originate, propagate, accumulate, and amplify in artificial intelligence models. It distinguishes three interacting sources of error: biases and limitations in training data, hallucinations, and context fading. Particular attention is paid to causal relationships between these error types and their implications for the reliability of AI-generated outputs. The presentation introduces methodological approaches to estimating error probabilities, assessing cumulative risks, and analyzing error propagation across reasoning steps, interconnected AI modules, and successive model generations. It discusses error reproduction, feedback mechanisms, and strategies for monitoring and mitigating systemic failures. The findings contribute to understanding AI reliability and risk assessment, particularly in applications involving cybersecurity, critical information infrastructure, and other high-stakes decision-making environments. Presented in connection with the V International Conference “Challenges and Reality of the IT-Space: Software Engineering and Cybersecurity” (SECS-2026), October 29–30, 2026, Kyiv, Ukraine (online).

title: Explainable Disease Classification via Multi-Ultrasound Images using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown promise in computer-aided diagnosis from multiple ultrasound images. However, their patient-level predictions do not reveal which images contribute to the result, limiting interpretability. We present an explanation framework that adapts Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) to graph-level prediction by perturbing each patient’s image set. Instead of superpixels, we sample image subsets, reconstruct their graphs, and estimate image-level influence. To generate informative perturbations, we propose a two-stage Adaptive Class-Balanced Sampling: Stage I samples randomly, and Stage II employs class-biased sampling, drawing 85% of images from the minority class pool to ensure an informative design matrix. Ridge and 10-fold cross-validated Elastic Net quantify conditional influence, while Pearson correlation describes marginal association. We evaluated the framework on 135 positive-label patients with 3,072 ultrasound images from the Taiwan Biobank. Adaptive sampling moved predicted class proportions closer to balance in 126 patients, but random sampling yielded lower mean Ridge probability-surrogate error (0.066 versus 0.119). For both sampling schemes, deleting images in descending coefficient order lowered model output more than random deletion in all patients. The framework provides image-level visual explanations and a statistical basis for examining how sampling, approximation and ranking contribute to interpretation of multi-image predictions.

title: Klasifikasi Sentimen Pengguna Platform X Terhadap Isu Geopolitik Israel–Palestina Menggunakan BERT
abstract: The geopolitical issue between Israel and Palestine has sparked a wide range of public reactions on social media, particularly on the platform X. Sentiment analysis is a widely discussed topic in Natural Language Processing. This study develops a sentiment classification model for that issue using the BERT Base Uncased architecture, with data labeled automatically through the VADER approach. Data were collected via scraping with Tweet-Harvest, yielding 3.172 tweets, later reduced to 2.362 after preprocessing stages including cleaning, case folding, tokenizing, stopword removal, and stemming. VADER labeling produced a distribution of 73.7% negative sentiment and 26.3% positive sentiment. The model achieved 86.92% accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-Score for the negative class of 90%, 93%, and 91%, respectively, while the positive class obtained 77%, 71%, and 74%. The average F1-score reached 88%. These results indicate the model correctly predicts most of the data, although a slight indication of overfitting appeared, with no significant impact on validation accuracy. This confirms that combining VADER and BERT Base Uncased is effective for sentiment classification on international geopolitical issues.

title: Integrating Linguistic Features with IndoBERT for Detecting Underage-Associated Comments in Indonesian YouTube
abstract: Indonesia has issued Government Regulation No. 17 of 2025 on Electronic System Governance for Child Protection (PP TUNAS), which prohibits independent access to digital platforms for individuals under 16. However, age verification remains difficult since users may provide fake birth dates during registration. This study aims to develop a hybrid text classification framework that integrates IndoBERT contextual embeddings with eight handcrafted linguistic features (teen_score, adult_score, emotion_score, grammar_score, word_count, exclamation_count, question_count, and teen_adult_ratio) to identify underage-associated comments on Indonesian YouTube. This study collected 37,450 comments from 271 videos using the YouTube Data API v3 and validated annotation consistency through manual labeling of 500 stratified samples, achieving Cohen's Kappa of 0.853 (almost perfect agreement). To address severe class imbalance, in which under-16 samples accounted for only 1.64%, then applied stratified 5-fold cross-validation with weighted sampling. The hybrid model achieved F1-scores of 0.7777 ± 0.0680 (cross-validation) and 0.9609 (test set). Ablation experiments confirmed explicit age disclosures are essential for the current annotation strategy. Although no significant performance difference was observed versus IndoBERT-only (p = 0.5743), the hybrid model provides explicit linguistic evidence through SHAP and LIME analyses, substantially improving interpretability. This makes the proposed framework suitable for transparent policy-oriented comment screening under PP TUNAS.

title: Intraoperative margin assessment in colorectal cancer via AI-enhanced multiphoton microscopy
abstract: Significance: Identifying residual tumors at the resection margins is crucial for individuals undergoing colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Accurate margin assessment can help minimize residual tumor while avoiding unnecessary removal of healthy tissue. Aim: This study uses label-free multiphoton microscopy to visualize collagen architecture and develops a feature-enhanced deep-learning model to distinguish CRC from margin-adjacent normal tissue. Approach: Margin-adjacent normal and carcinoma tissues were imaged using multiphoton microscopy, and 142 quantitative collagen features were extracted from SHG images. We propose PVT-Enhanced, a feature-fusion model that integrates handcrafted collagen features with deep image features derived from PVTv2-b5 through an attention-based fusion strategy. Its performance was compared with LASSO-LR, three convolutional neural networks, and image-only PVTv2-b5. Results: SHG imaging showed relatively coherent fiber orientation, longer and more continuous collagen fibers, and higher fiber density in margin-adjacent normal tissue, whereas carcinoma tissue showed more disorganized orientation, shorter and more fragmented fibers, and lower fiber density. The PVT-Enhanced model achieved an accuracy of 86.9%, an AUC of 0.923, and a specificity of 96.4%. Only 5 of 137 margin-adjacent normal images were misclassified as CRC. Conclusions: Our findings suggest that the PVT-Enhanced framework combined with SHG imaging allows accurate, rapid, and label-free tissue characterization that may support intraoperative margin assessment in CRC surgery.

title: Affective directions in activation space: An interpretable inference-time control mechanism
abstract: Emotion is a fundamental component of human communication, shaping understanding, trust, and engagement across domains such as education, healthcare, and mental health. Although large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong reasoning and knowledge-generation capabilities, they still struggle to express emotions in a consistent, controllable, and contextually appropriate manner. This limitation restricts their potential for authentic human–AI interaction. We propose a controllable emotion generation framework based on Emotion Vectors (EVs) —latent representations derived from internal activation shifts between neutral and emotion-conditioned responses. By injecting these vectors into the hidden states of pretrained LLMs during inference, our method enables fine-grained, continuous modulation of emotional tone without any additional training or architectural modification. We further provide a first-order theoretical analysis of emotional steering and its interaction with a semantic readout under explicit local assumptions. Experiments across multiple LLM families demonstrate adjustable emotional expression and characterize the model-dependent trade-off between steering strength, topical relevance, and fluency. The framework provides a general, training-free control interface with explicit intensity scaling and vector composition. Comparisons with prompting and fine-tuning characterize the emotional and quality effects of the evaluated configurations. Emotion Vector (EV) steering thus offers an efficient and interpretable means of bridging rational reasoning and affective understanding in large language models, and points to a promising direction for building emotionally resonant AI systems capable of more natural human–machine interaction.

title: EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference
abstract: Foundation models like V-JEPA are increasingly deployed across a heterogeneous edge-cloud continuum spanning smart glasses, phones, robots, and servers. Yet, they are typically trained as rigid, fixed-capacity networks bound to one device, supporting neither reconfigurable compute budgets nor collaborative execution. Existing approaches address only one axis at a time: slimmable and NAS-based methods provide width elasticity but assume single-device inference, whereas split-computing methods enable cross-device collaboration only for fixed partitions and static capacities. We introduce Elastic V-JEPA (EV-JEPA), a single model trained once and deployable everywhere along the continuum. Its width is reconfigurable, and it is natively partitionable across heterogeneous devices. At its core is Transition-Aware Triplet Training (T3). At each step we pick a narrow and a wide width, and train three paths: each width alone, plus a hybrid path that runs the early layers narrow and the rest wide. The hybrid switch point is where one device hands off to another, so the same weights learn both single-device and cross-device execution. Across various benchmarks, EV-JEPA falls within 1 accuracy point of independently trained baselines while improving over previous elastic training approaches by up to 11 accuracy points. Narrow-to-wide cross-device hybrid execution recovers to within 1.1 points of the highest-capacity standalone model and supports many-to-one, any-to-any, and variable-split configurations. Finally, we show that the elastic principle extends beyond the backbone to an elastic token compression mechanism that exposes controllable trade-offs among on-device computation, latency, and accuracy.

title: Spanning Diffusion and Flow-based Posterior Sampling via Exact Gaussian Conditioning
abstract: Flow-matching and diffusion models are increasingly used as priors for linear inverse problems, however, most methods are bespoke to one class of trajectory prior. Plug-and-play methods have been proposed, however these implicitly decorrelate the guided trajectory, resulting in broad priors that can struggle when data is sparse. This work proposes $β$-Flow: a general plug-and-play method indexed by a correlation parameter $β$ that generalises over flow, diffusion, and decorrelated priors, and a confidence parameter $κ$ that controls how strongly the path distribution is enforced. Each step requires only one forward evaluation of a denoising network, followed by a Gaussian conditioning step. This step is an exact Kalman update that is not dependent on network gradients. We show that many existing guided samplers can be interpreted as instances or approximations of our method, each implicitly using a different trajectory prior and operator in place of the Kalman gain. From this viewpoint, we provide a qualitative comparison of methods in terms of their implicit biases and assumptions. We demonstrate consistently state-of-the-art level performance across 7 inverse problems over 4 datasets in terms of PSNR and SSIM. Moreover, we demonstrate the utility of this prior control, by showing that confident high correlations (strict priors) work best when observations are less informative, while low correlation is preferred when observations are more informative, reflecting the complementary roles of the prior and likelihood in Bayesian inference.

title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels
abstract: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. We propose JEPA-kMMVAE, which combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict future CSI through temporally structured latent representations. The framework supports direct prediction and residual corrections relative to the latest latent state and noisy CSI observation. Simulation results show that the residual configuration outperforms the evaluated baselines at moderate and high input CSI signal-to-noise ratios, while sequence baselines remain more accurate under stronger noise.

title: A7 — Operational Will. Commitment, Initiative, and the Question of What an Agent Does Next.
abstract: An agent can remember an obligation and still never return to it. A daily schedule can keep it busy while important work slips away. I call the missing capacity operational will: not a private feeling or a claim of personhood, but a system-level ability to carry legitimate commitments across pauses, initiate within their scope, reconsider attention, and explain both action and deliberate non-action. I propose a bounded architecture: persistent commitments, time and event signals, an active decision model, and an I-Entity, a read-only reviewer that asks questions but cannot command tools. Earlier work on intention and BDI agents already covers much of this territory; the contribution here is a separable, auditable cross-commitment review interface and a falsifiable way to test whether it improves decisions. Dated ZAI records supply difficult design cases: a blocked proposal queue, restraint after permission, and a scheduler that reported success without acting. A proposed seven-condition test asks whether broader attention actually improves decisions over ordinary checklists and critics; the evaluation has not yet been run.

A proposed seven-condition test asks whether broader attention actually improves decisions over ordinary checklists and critics; the evaluation has not yet been run.

title: IRCM-FS: Reproducibility Package for Compact and Stable Wrapper Feature Selection
abstract: This record provides the reproducibility package for IRCM-FS, a confidence-aware intervention–response contextual memory method for compact and stable wrapper feature selection. The package contains the frozen IRCM-FS implementation used in the independent benchmark, benchmark and baseline code, verification scripts, processed experimental results, statistical analysis outputs, reproducibility documentation, environment specifications, tests, and manuscript figure-generation scripts. The benchmark covers 11 public classification tasks, six methods, five random seeds, and 330 fresh runs under a common nominal evaluation budget. Raw UCI datasets are not redistributed and can be obtained from their original sources as documented in the package.

title: QOIDAVIY KKT FORMALIZMI VA YIRIK TIL MODELLARI INTEGRATSIYASI: ARXITEKTURA VARIANTLARI TASNIFI VA BAHOLASH MEZONLARI
abstract: Tezisda ijtimoiy ahamiyatli sohalar raqamlashtirilishi sharoitida kam resursli o‘zbek tili uchun qoidaviy mashina tarjimasi bilan yirik til modellarini (YTM) birlashtirish masalasi ko‘riladi. Prof. M. X. Hakimov ishlab chiqqan kengayuvchi kirish tili (KKT) formalizmiga asoslangan o‘zbekcha–inglizcha tizim negizida integratsiyaning olti arxitektura varianti yagona tasnifga keltiriladi. Tasnif ikki savolga javob beradi: har konfiguratsiyada KKT nima qiladi va YTM nima qiladi. Sof qoidaviy va sof neyron chegara-holatlardan tortib, YTM realizator, tahlil-iste’molchi, verifikatsiya sikli ostidagi tarjimon va yozma qoida-matn ijrochisi vazifasini bajaradigan konfiguratsiyalar ko‘rib chiqiladi; har biri uchun mehnat taqsimoti, kutiladigan afzallik va ishlash-sharti aniqlanadi. Tasnifga ortogonal ravishda tarjima vaqtidan tashqari yo‘nalish — tasdiq-darvozali oflayn resurs to‘ldirish — ajratiladi. Gibrid tizimlarni baholashda yagona avtomatik ball yetarli emasligi asoslanib, to‘rt o‘qli mezon ramkasi taklif etiladi: sifat, formalizm-sodiqlik, determinizm va terminologik izchillik. Miqdoriy taqqoslash natijalari oldindan ro‘yxatga olingan protokol asosida alohida ishda e’lon qilinadi.

title: ИССЛЕДОВАНИЕ ДАТАСЕТОВ ДЛЯ РАЗДЕЛЕНИЯ ИСТОЧНИКОВ РЕЧИ И ИЗУЧЕНИЕ ВЛИЯНИЯ КРИТЕРИЕВ КАЧЕСТВА ДАННЫХ НА ОБУЧЕНИЕ
abstract: Данная статья исследует датасеты для разделения источников речи, оценивая объективные критерии качества и разнообразия данных, а также оценивает влияние каждого критерия на эффективность обучения, что может быть полезным для дальнейшей разработки или модификации данных для работы с речью. Были рассмотрены базовые критерии качества данных, а также характеристики, которые можно оценить статистически. Для оценки качества разделения, датасеты были обучены на нейросетевых моделях, и протестированы на общем тестовом наборе данных. Была проведена оценка влияния медианной составляющей и разброса в каждом критерии на качество разделения, а также с помощью количественной оценки корреляции в виде критерия Пирсона. Итоговый результат показал, что сильнее всего качеством модели положительно коррелирует средний процент речи и перекрытия двух спикеров.

title: Online comprehensive identification algorithm for seafloor hydrothermal plumes based on anomaly detection
abstract: The detection of hydrothermal plumes is crucial for discovering active seafloor hydrothermal fields and exploring seafloor resources. To enable autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to adapt their survey strategies in real time, this study proposes an integrated online identification algorithm that couples real-time anomaly detection with fluid-type classification using deep learning models trained on historical data from the Qianlong-II AUV. The algorithm combines sliding-window statistical features, gated recurrent unit networks for sensor-specific anomaly detection, and a multi-layer perceptron that fuses the anomaly probabilities to classify the fluid types of the plumes. Training labels are generated by offline algorithms tailored to different anomaly types, K-medoids clustering for point anomalies (temperature, turbidity) and adaptive iterative fitting for subsequence anomalies (methane, oxidation-reduction potential). Experimental evaluation under a leave-one-field-out protocol demonstrates that the online algorithm replicates the offline labeling logic with 98.67% fidelity, with ablation studies confirming the critical contribution of the anomaly detection stage. The proposed algorithm offers an effective, real-time deployable solution for autonomous hydrothermal exploration, significantly enhancing AUVs’ operational autonomy.

title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong results in classical code generation and are increasingly used to write the unit tests that safeguard that code. Whether they can do the same for quantum software is less clear, because quantum programs are probabilistic, depend on numerical tolerances, and are judged by domain-specific checkers, so a well-formed test can still disagree with the benchmark's verdict. Existing quantum benchmarks measure whether a model produces a correct solution, but not whether its tests can distinguish correct implementations from faulty ones. We introduce QTestBench, a framework that evaluates LLM-generated quantum test suites against independent benchmark checkers, never treating the tests themselves as ground truth. For each task, QTestBench prompts models to produce syntactic, semantic, and behavioral tests, injects candidate solutions at runtime, and compares each test verdict with the checker's label under three validation cohorts, each answering a distinct diagnostic question. We benchmark five LLMs on eight PennyLane QHack challenges and ten Qiskit HumanEval tasks. Generated suites almost always execute, but discrimination lags behind: the best generator reaches a test quality of 0.71 on QHack and 0.34 on Qiskit HumanEval, so executability alone overstates test quality. Oracle-verified synthetic mutants stabilize bug-detection estimates when natural faulty solutions are scarce, as on three of ten Qiskit tasks that yield none. QTestBench offers a reproducible, cross-framework benchmark for the trustworthiness of LLM-generated quantum tests.

title: NovaSplat: Model-Free 6D Object Pose Estimation via 3D Gaussian Splatting Onboarding and Refinement
abstract: 6D pose estimation of novel objects without CAD models remains an open challenge: model-free methods must build the object representation from scratch during onboarding and have long trailed their model-based counterparts. We present NovaSplat, a model-free pipeline that closes this gap. From a short smartphone video captured at onboarding, we train a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model that serves both as a template source for detection and coarse pose estimation and as a differentiable backbone for pose refinement. Our refiner optimizes the object-to-camera pose with combined photometric and geometric losses under a continuous rotation parametrization free of gradient singularities. On a household-object benchmark, NovaSplat surpasses all model-based methods. On a challenging industrial benchmark with textureless and specular surfaces, it outperforms all model-free competitors while substantially narrowing the gap to model-based ones. We further introduce NovaSplat-Lite, an inference variant that is $3.1\times$ faster at negligible accuracy cost. Code will be made available at \href{https://github.com/POSE-Lab/novasplat}{https://github.com/POSE-Lab/novasplat}.

title: Universal Bounds for Self-Normalized Kullback-Leibler Estimation
abstract: This work studies an entropy-based estimator of Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence constructed from normalized importance weights. We prove a universal finite-sample bound showing that its expectation can exceed the target-proposal KL divergence by at most $\log 2$ for any sample size. We then characterize the KL divergence between the distribution induced by importance-weighted resampling and the proposal, showing that it is upper bounded by both the expectation of the entropy-based estimator and the target-proposal KL divergence. Importantly, these bounds require neither bounded importance weights nor finite higher moments. We apply these results to test-time alignment of generative models via Soft Best-of-$N$ sampling, an importance-sampling-based scaling technique proposed by Verdun et al. (2025), and to relative entropy coding, obtaining finite-sample policy-divergence certificates and moment-free bounds on coding cost.

title: A Scalable Clustering-Based Approach for Efficient Mining of Large Datasets
authors: Harshita Koushal, Dr. Harsh Lohiya, Mr. Manoj Kumar Yadav
abstract: Clustering is an unsupervised machine learning technique used to identify and group similar data points within large datasets without relying on predefined class labels or target outcomes. It plays an important role in data mining by facilitating the discovery of meaningful groups, hidden patterns, and relevant data distributions. Traditional clustering methods generally assume that clusters are spherical and have relatively similar sizes, which can reduce their effectiveness when dealing with irregularly shaped clusters or datasets containing outliers. To address the challenges associated with clustering large databases, several approaches employ random sampling and partitioning techniques. In such methods, a large dataset is first divided into smaller partitions, and each partition is clustered independently. The resulting partial clusters are subsequently combined and clustered again to generate the final set of clusters. This approach reduces the computational burden associated with processing the entire dataset simultaneously. With the rapid growth of data volumes, several parallel clustering techniques based on the Map Reduce framework have also been proposed to improve scalability. However, applying the conventional K-Means algorithm to large datasets in a parallel environment may require the repeated reading and processing of data during each iteration. Consequently, this iterative process can significantly increase input/output operations and network communication overhead. To overcome these limitations, a series-based K-Means clustering approach, referred to as CBK Means, can be employed to reduce the amount of data processed while maintaining or improving clustering quality. The method uses representative data verification to effectively reduce the dataset size before or during the clustering process. Experimental results indicate that CBK Means provides improved efficiency and scalability compared with the conventional K-Means algorithm, while also achieving better clustering accuracy.

title: A Competence-Based Architecture for Personalized Adaptive Learning
abstract: Traditional e-learning systems often provide limited personalization and adaptation to individual student needs. This paper presents a competence-based architecture for personalized adaptive learning in higher education that integrates an ontology-based content model, practical-skill verification, a learning-analytics-based student model, and explainable adaptive recommendations. The novelty lies in integrating these components into a single assessment-driven architecture in which a competence-and-depth content ontology, a mastery-and-attainment student model, and an ontology-grounded explainable recommendation layer operate together on real course data. The architecture was evaluated as a proof of concept using records from two undergraduate computing courses representing different computing subdomains. Student activity and assessment data were used to estimate mastery, distinguish demonstrated competence mastery from depth-level attainment, and generate prerequisite-aware recommendations from ontology relations. The results show that the proposed approach provides interpretable mastery estimates and ontology-grounded recommendations, offering initial evidence for the feasibility of competence-based adaptive learning in real course settings. A student feedback survey (n = 86) indicated positive perceptions of the clarity, relevance, and usefulness of the generated recommendations. The main contribution is a working, interpretable pipeline that transforms verified assessment evidence into mastery estimates, behavioral student types, and explainable learning recommendations.

title: Preregistration: Block IV Adaptive Agency and Structural Generalisation - Theory of Everything Research Programme.
abstract: This preregistration freezes the first confirmatory study for Experimental Block IV of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. Block IV tests whether artificial agents can adapt to previously unseen causal structures, compositions and problem families, and whether explicit predictive modelling and counterfactual rollout make selective causal contributions beyond serious model-free and heuristic alternatives. Seven hypotheses (H4.1-H4.7), twenty held-out seeds, confirmatory-only structural task variants, architecture classes, compute/storage matching rules, model-corruption and correction interventions, primary estimands, thresholds and Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Suspend/Reject rules are frozen before confirmatory execution. Development-only simulations were used to validate the implementation and choose prospective thresholds; their outcomes are disclosed and excluded from confirmatory evidence. No Block IV confirmatory seed had been executed when the protocol was frozen. A positive result would support only scoped causal contributions to structural generalisation in the registered artificial environments. It would not establish general intelligence, universal necessity of world models, reflective self-awareness or phenomenal consciousness. Related methodological framework: Craggs, K. (2026), Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230.

title: DASL-Net: adaptive streaming learning for robust robot perception under concept drift
abstract: Robots operating in dynamic environments often encounter concept drift caused by sensor noise, environmental changes, mechanical wear, and evolving task requirements, which can degrade perception and decision-making performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes DASL-Net, an adaptive streaming learning network for robust robot perception under concept drift. DASL-Net enables robots to continuously update their perception models from streaming sensory data while preserving previously learned knowledge. The network adaptively deepens existing branches for gradual concept evolution and creates new branches for emerging concepts. To reduce catastrophic forgetting and negative interference, DASL-Net uses Fisher information to measure the importance of historical parameters and guides branch generation by comparing Fisher information with current gradients. Experiments on multiple streaming classification benchmarks show that DASL-Net achieves better adaptability and long-term accuracy than conventional deep learning and incremental learning methods, demonstrating its potential for reliable robot perception in non-stationary environments.

title: Motion uncertainty visualization based on Gaussian process regression
abstract: In the context of image-guided soft-tissue intervention and surgery navigation, soft tissue motion estimation for a deformed/registered pre-operative/pre-interventional medical image may suffer from multiple sources of uncertainty. Visualizing the uncertainty in the deformed image is of great interest because it conveys the uncertainty in the registered pre-interventional/pre-operative navigation information on deformable soft-tissue organs governing the decisions of the surgeon or intervention specialist. We address the problem of propagating the uncertainty from a Gaussian process (GP)-based motion estimation of an input image. To visualize the deformed image itself, we show its maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate. To convey the overall uncertainty in the MAP deformed image estimate, we apply a spatially-varying blur (according to the uncertain motion estimate) to an image containing a grid and combine it with the MAP deformed image itself. We show 2D cross sections of the final image that convey both the deformed image and its uncertainty. We further extend our approach to local investigations of points or regions of interest (e.g., a tumor). To visualize where a point/region of interest (POI/ROI) is after deformation, we estimate marginal (i.e., per voxel) label (e.g., for being a tumor) probabilities (MLPs) based on an input probabilistic segmentation of the ROI in the non-deformed pre-interventional/pre-operative image and the input GP posterior distribution over deformation fields and show 2D cross sections of visually mapped MLPs or MLP isocontours.

title: MvFFN: Multi-view Floor plan Feed-forward Network for Unposed Wide-Baseline Panorama Layout Reconstruction
abstract: Reconstructing accurate camera poses and floor-plan layouts from sparse, unposed, wide-baseline RGB panoramas remains a challenging open problem. Direct multi-room floor-plan prediction is especially difficult in this setting: pose, geometry, semantics, and global layout structure are tightly coupled, yet a complete floor-plan is hard to learn as a single global output. Our key insight is to keep the model's predictions strictly local. Multi-view Ordered Wall Instance Segmentation (MOIS) is designed around this concept. Each panorama column predicts only the wall it observes plus the next two adjacent walls in clockwise order. The global wall partition, room layouts, and shared coordinates emerge from deterministic aggregation of overlapping local predictions. Building on MOIS, we propose Multi-view floor-plan Feed-Forward Network (MvFFN), which jointly predicts coarse camera poses, dense global geometry, and per-wall semantic outputs. A downstream Layout Chaining (LC) post processing pipeline then assembles these predictions into multi-room floor-plans with shared global coordinates, consistent wall identities, and connected room structure. The dense MOIS predictions recover cross-view wall identity and local within-room connectivity more accurately than composed modular baselines, and the assembled layouts substantially outperform prior methods on wall and junction level accuracy. We also introduce the ZInD-CrossView dataset, which augments ZInD with globally unique wall instances and cross-view segmentation labels for this task.

title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are now a standard source of query expansion terms but they hallucinate. They inject non existent entities and off-topic terms that add ranking noise and can hurt strong retrievers. Existing remedies such as corpus grounding, mutual verification and preference alignment treat hallucinated terms as an undifferentiated nuisance to be filtered by agreement heuristics, without a mechanistic account of why a given term appears or a principled criterion for how many terms to keep. We propose Subsequence-Association Filtered, breadth-aware query expansion (SAFE-QE), a training-free, retriever agnostic method that draws on the subsequence-association account of hallucination. We score each candidate expansion term by its corpus conditioned cross-context reproducibility, terms that reappear under randomised query contexts yet lack support in the pseudo-relevant set are flagged as products of dominant hallucinatory associations and down-weighted. Drawing on the characterisation of language generation as a trade-off between consistency (no hallucination) and breadth (coverage), we cast term selection as constrained coverage maximisation over the pseudo-relevant set, keeping a set that is approximately broad but consistent and stable across resampling. We also introduce the Hallucinated Expansion Term Rate, a query side faithfulness metric that counts injected expansion terms no relevant document supports. We evaluate our approach on benchmarked TREC and BEIR collections. Our SAFE-QE is statistically indistinguishable from generative and corpus-steered expansion on nDCG@10 while injecting fewer unsupported terms 4.3 per query against 27.8 for Query2doc and 57.5 for HyDE and on a strong learned sparse retriever, where every expansion method regresses. Faithfulness is therefore available at no measurable cost in ranking quality.

title: Correlation-Based Measurement of Entanglement in Rank-2 Mixed States
abstract: We study correlation-based entanglement evaluation in rank-2 mixed states of two- and multi-qubit systems. The relevant two-dimensional subspace is treated as a logical qubit embedded in the physical Hilbert space, and factorizable realizations of its logical Pauli operators are classified. For two qubits, this yields nontrivial canonical encodings related by local Clifford transformations. The relation between logical and physical Bloch vectors admits a geometric interpretation as a transversely deformed Bloch sphere, leading to closed-form expressions for two-qubit concurrence and generalized concurrence across $N$-qubit bipartitions. The entanglement scaling factor is obtained directly from complementary-subsystem correlations, without prior calibration of state-preparation parameters. Noisy simulations using the IBM Quantum FakeKingston backend model, with readout-error mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation, confirm the analytical results up to $N=10$ qubits. The protocol therefore enables entanglement estimation from only a small number of measurement settings for this class of rank-2 logical states.

title: RARA: Robust Policy Fine-Tuning through Retrieval-Anchored Representation Alignment for Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Pre-trained robot policies, such as Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, provide a strong foundation for generalist robotic manipulation, but adapting them to new tasks with only a few demonstrations remains challenging. Directly fine-tuning a pre-trained policy often achieves strong in-distribution performance, yet it can distort the representations learned during pre-training and weaken the model's generalization ability under out-of-distribution shifts. We propose Retrieval-Anchored Representation Alignment (RARA), a two-stage adaptation method, to address this issue. First, RARA retrieves representation features from pretraining with similar task intent and motion, and aligns the policy's representations of the target demonstrations with the pre-trained representations of the retrieved demonstrations. Second, RARA fine-tunes the policy on the target demonstrations while limiting how much its representations of the retrieved demonstrations change during fine-tuning. By reducing the representation mismatch before action learning and preserving pre-trained knowledge during adaptation, RARA limits unnecessary representation drift during fine-tuning. Experiments with Diffusion Policy and GR00T on 13 tasks in RoboTwin, RoboCasa, and on a real robot show that RARA improves the average success of fine-tuning by 9.5 points in-distribution and 13.6 points out-of-distribution, and outperforms all compared baselines. Project page: https://shua-kang.github.io/RARA_robot/

title: Sustainable Cloud-Fog-Edge Systems for Smart Buildings: Algorithmic Adaptation under Memory Constraints and Dynamic Orchestration Strategies
abstract: The escalating environmental footprint of the Information and Communication Technol- ogy (ICT) sectorwith global Data Center electric- ity usage potentially reaching 3% by 2030 and the imperative for real-time responsiveness in smart buildings demand a foundational shift towards Edge Computing. This article proposes a holis- tic architectural and algorithmic approach for cre- ating autonomous, resilient, and privacy-preserving learning systems within smart buildings, advancing the core concept of the building itself as the data center. Our contributions, demonstrating originality compared to conventional centralized systems, are structured around three main pillars: 1) Validation of resilient data acquisition chains using the af- fordable Arduino ecosystem (Uno R4 WiFi/BME280) and secure persistence solutions including centralized archiving (Node-RED/MySQL) and secure remote transfer (Python/rsync/SSH). 2). The proposal of a lightweight, KOptim orchestration framework, inter- operable with the FIWARE standard, for the dynamic management of Service Level Agreements (SLA). 3) The adaptation and experimental valida- tion of the Generalized Hebbian Algorithm (GHA) for Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on low- power microcontrollers,We introduce and compare an iterative learning strategy using data buffers, featuring sorting and explicit preservation of extreme samples to maintain diversity. Experimental results on the high-dimensional Tour Perret sensor data confirm that this novel method, despite introducing a necessary temporal complexity of O(W log W ) due to sorting, achieves convergence and final result quality that is visually equivalent to processing the entire dataset in full memory, reliably identifying two distinct operational states.
